title.en: HRM, job analysis and manpower planning

heading.en: The right people in the right jobs

hook.en: A hospital is opening a new wing next year. How many nurses will it need, with what skills, and how many of today's staff will still be there? Human resource management starts with these questions.

objectives.en: Explain the meaning and functions of HRM
Explain job analysis, job description and job specification

narration.en: A hospital is opening a new wing next year. How many nurses will it need, with what skills, and how many of today's staff will still be there? Human resource management starts with these questions.

body.en: Human resource management is the part of management concerned with acquiring, developing, using and keeping a competent and satisfied workforce. Its functions include manpower planning, recruitment and selection, placement and induction, training and development, performance appraisal, compensation, internal mobility (promotion and transfer), separation, welfare and industrial relations. It starts with job analysis: a systematic study of a job to find its duties and the qualities needed to do it. Job analysis produces a job description (what the job involves: title, duties, responsibilities, conditions) and a job specification (who can do it: qualifications, experience, skills and personal qualities).

points.en: HRM: acquire, develop, use and retain people
Job analysis: study of a job's contents and requirements

title.en: On the board: A manpower plan

say.en: Workload next year: 1,80,000 hours. Each employee works 2,000 hours, less 10% absence.
There are 90 staff today and 12 percent are expected to leave.

text.en: Plan: recruit 21 people before the year starts.

body.en: Manpower (human resource) planning estimates the number and kind of people the organisation will need in future and plans how to get them. Its steps are: forecasting the demand for people from workload and plans; estimating the supply from present staff after allowing for retirements, resignations and promotions; finding the gap; and planning action: recruitment if there is a shortage, or transfers, redeployment or separation if there is a surplus. It avoids both shortages and surpluses of staff, and supports recruitment, training and succession.

points.en: Action: recruit, train, transfer or separate
